content: This document provides a summary of information about a product but does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your use. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace consultation with your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before using streptomycin injection, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other aminoglycoside antibiotics (such as tobramycin or gentamicin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Streptomycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as BCG or typhoid vaccines). Notify your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as you should not become pregnant while using streptomycin. This medication may harm an unborn baby. Additionally, streptomycin passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has instructed you to take low doses of aspirin (typically 81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking the aspirin as directed. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney function, hearing tests, and streptomycin levels) should be conducted regularly. If you miss a dose, it is important to receive the medication as scheduled. Store unmixed medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
